The X peoples, specifically the Y speakers, are believed to have introduced early rice cultivation to India, migrating from Southeast Asia/southern China around 2000 BCE. They brought specialized agricultural knowledge, utilizing both wet and dry cultivation techniques, and profoundly influenced agricultural terminology in early Indian languages. Their rice varieties and cultivation techniques, coupled with the ones which were already existent in India, played an important role in ensuring that rice cultivation expanded in scope and quality in the Indian subcontinent ‎
